title: Guidance
description: How to define one kind well, in one language: what it is in the discipline's words, what each field asks for with a right and a wrong example, what to ask when a link is missing, and how to meet each check. A person reads it beside the editor; an agent reads it before drafting. It holds words only: the steps, fields, links and checks are the flow's and the engine's, so a language is added by adding a bundle, and no rule depends on one. Examples are drawn from the fictional cooperative in examples/minimal, so every reader learns from the same model.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag of the words, such as en or fr-CA.

definition.description: What this kind is, in the discipline's words (TAXONOMY.md), and what it is not.

levels.description: For a kind with levels (Goal: goal, objective, outcome): what each level is, as a dictionary gives it, in one plain sentence that does not repeat the level's name.

levelExamples.description: For a kind with levels: one real instance of each level, held to the same rule as example.

terms.description: Other words this kind holds that a person meets on screen, each defined as summary and example are (TAXONOMY.md D29): a project's component, say. The glossary lists them after the kind.

steps.description: By step key: the step's title and guide in this language, where they differ from the flow's.

fields.description: By the field's JSON pointer, as the flow and the schema name it (list items as /spec/keyResults/-/metric).

links.description: By Kind:/path, as the flow's link names it: what to ask when establishing the link, and what to do when there is nothing to link to.

checks.description: By check id: how to meet it, in a sentence.

judgements.description: Checks a decision model answers, where one is configured (docs/adr/0023), keyed by check id. Each is a contrast read off the field's good and poor examples: the text is placed between a good option and a poor one, asked good first, and the check is met when the good option is more likely. A contrast is kept only once it has been measured against examples whose answer is known (the ADR records how); without a model none is asked, and nothing else changes.

path.description: The field, by JSON pointer; - for every item of a list.

levels.description: For a kind with levels, the levels it is asked at; all when left out.

key.description: A plain word naming the option; the model reads it.

label.description: What the option is, in a few words.

key.description: A plain word naming the option; the model reads it.

label.description: What the option is, in a few words.

fail.description: What to say when the poor option is more likely; {n} is the item's number in a list.

cues.description: How a decision model recognises a text a person typed as this kind (docs/adr/0023), by stage key. Asked of each stage on its own, good option first, against "something else"; the three likeliest stages are offered to the person, who chooses. A stage with levels and no cue is asked by its level's definition (levels), the same words a person reads, and its level is chosen among them. Changed only with a new measurement against sentences whose stage is known.

vocabulary.description: Words an interface offers to help write a field in this language, such as the verbs an aim opens with or the word that introduces an objective's means. Offered, never used to judge: no check or mark depends on them, and a language without them gets plain fields.

summary.description: What the kind is, as a dictionary gives it, for a person meeting the word for the first time: one plain sentence in everyday words that does not repeat the kind's name, and names no standard, field or identifier (TAXONOMY.md D29). Shown wherever a list of kinds names it, beside a "?" where the word appears, and in the glossary.

example.description: One real instance of the kind, from the example workspace, that shows every part the summary names (a gap's state today and the state it should reach, not only one) in words a newcomer knows. Shown under the summary.

knownAs.description: What plans and documents often call this kind instead, in this language: for recognising one, never for naming it. A document's word is mapped by what the thing is, against the definition, so a plan's "objective" may be an outcome here, and the kind's own name is always used.

guide.description: What the field asks for, in the discipline's words.

good.description: Values written as the discipline would.

poor.description: Values that read plausibly and are wrong, each with why.

levels.description: For a kind with levels: the guide and examples for one level, where they differ.
